title: Predictive Maintenance & Inspection Checklists
contentStatus: Draft for DiFacto review. Title and content to be confirmed.

sections.title: Predictive Versus Preventive
learningObjectives: Distinguish predictive maintenance from the preventive maintenance covered in Module 2
Understand why predictive maintenance requires closer observation, not just scheduling
sections.content: Where preventive maintenance follows a set schedule (based on time and usage) regardless of condition, predictive maintenance is triggered by actual signs of degradation - a component wearing faster than typical, a performance metric drifting from its normal range. This requires closer, ongoing observation rather than just following a schedule.

keyTerms.note: Maintenance triggered by actual signs of wear or drift, rather than by the calendar.
The gradual loss of performance or condition in a component over time.

video.title: Predictive or preventive in 30 seconds
video.transcript: Predictive or preventive? Preventive maintenance follows a set schedule. It runs regardless of condition. Predictive acts on actual signs of degradation. A component wearing faster than typical. A metric drifting from its normal range. That takes closer, ongoing observation.

sections.title: Signs Worth Watching For
learningObjectives: Understand general categories of early warning signs
Recognize that predictive indicators are often subtle, not dramatic
sections.content: Predictive signs tend to be gradual rather than sudden: slightly increased noise or vibration from a drive component, a battery charging cycle that takes marginally longer than it used to, a sensor reading that's technically within range but trending in one direction over time. None of these individually demand immediate action - but tracked over time, they indicate when proactive attention is worthwhile.

keyTerms.note: Rapid back-and-forth movement; a change in a drive component's vibration can signal wear.
A pattern of readings moving steadily in one direction over time.

sections.title: Using Inspection Checklists Effectively
learningObjectives: Understand the purpose of a structured inspection checklist
Recognize how to use a checklist as a tool for comparison over time, not just a one-time pass/fail
sections.content: An inspection checklist's real value comes from consistency over time - recording actual values (not just pass/fail) where possible, so this inspection can be compared against the last one. A checklist that only records 'OK' or 'not OK' misses the gradual trends that predictive maintenance depends on noticing. Specific checklist items for MoRo's inspection points will be confirmed against DiFacto documentation.

keyTerms.note: A list of inspection points a technician checks and records at each visit.

sections.title: Interpreting Trend Data
learningObjectives: Know that reading a trend across inspections is a skill that comes with experience
Recognize the difference between normal variation and a meaningful trend
sections.content: A single reading rarely tells you much; a series of readings over several inspections can reveal whether something is stable (normal variation) or trending in a concerning direction. Technicians need to distinguish ordinary fluctuation from a genuine trend - this comes with experience and with having consistent, comparable data to work from, which is exactly why consistent checklist use matters.

sections.title: Deciding When to Act
learningObjectives: Understand that the decision to act sits between acting on every fluctuation and acting too late
Recognize the trade-off between acting too early and too late
sections.content: Acting too early on every minor fluctuation wastes maintenance resources on components that would have continued performing fine; acting too late risks the failure predictive maintenance was meant to prevent. The judgment call sits between these - informed by trend data, component-specific knowledge, and operational context (how critical is this unit right now, how soon can it be scheduled for attention).

sections.title: Connecting to Diagnostic Work
learningObjectives: Understand how predictive observation connects to the diagnostic methodology in later modules
Recognize this module's place in building toward full diagnostic competency
sections.content: Predictive maintenance and diagnostic troubleshooting (covered later in this track) share a common foundation: both depend on recognizing what's normal well enough to notice deviation. The difference is timing - predictive work catches issues before they become operational problems; diagnostics (Module 5) responds once something has already gone wrong. Both skills reinforce each other.

questions.question: Which is a predictive trigger?
options: A check reaching its scheduled due point
A performance metric drifting from its normal range
A component that has stopped working
questions.feedback: Correct. Predictive maintenance responds to observed signs of degradation, not to a schedule or a failure.

questions.question: Which is a typical predictive sign, as the lesson describes them?
options: A unit that will not power on
A charging cycle taking marginally longer than it used to
questions.feedback: Correct. Predictive indicators are usually subtle trends, not dramatic single events.

questions.question: A reading has been recorded as 'OK' at each of the last four inspections. What can't you tell?
options: Whether it is trending in one direction
questions.feedback: Correct. A pass or fail does not show a trend. Recorded values can be compared over time to spot gradual change.

questions.question: Which pair names the two errors the lesson warns about?
options: Recording values, and recording pass or fail
Acting on every minor fluctuation, and acting too late
Inspecting too often, and documenting too much
questions.feedback: Correct. Acting on every minor fluctuation wastes resources; acting too late risks the failure predictive maintenance is meant to prevent.

questions.question: What is the main difference between predictive work and diagnostics?
options: Only diagnostics needs knowledge of what is normal
Timing: predictive work acts before an operational problem, diagnostics after something has gone wrong
Predictive work needs no recorded data
questions.feedback: Correct. Both skills share the same foundation of recognizing normal versus abnormal.
